title: Part Four, Chapter 11: The Houses of the Gods and the Fasts

verses.t: And now we shall tell again the name of the house of the god; for its house was likewise named with the name of the god. The Great Building of Tohil was the name of the building of his house. Tohil, of the people of Caviquib, was the name of the building; the house of Avilix, of the people of Nihaibab; and Hacavitz was the name of the building of the house of the god of the people of Ahan-Quiché. Tzutuha, which is seen at Cahbaha, was the name of another building, where the stone was that all the lords and all the peoples worshipped. And first the offering was brought, and then afterwards they went to give their tributes to the king; and this lord was supported and fed by the chiefs who had conquered the peoples. And King Cucumatz and Cotuha were great lords and diviners and naguals, and Quicab and Cavizimah were naguals as well. And they knew whether there would be war, and it was plain to them, and they saw everything: whether there would be death, or famine, or strife; they knew everything. And there was a place where they saw everything, a book of everything, which they called the Book of the Community. And the lords were not so for nothing, for their being was a great thing, and great were their fasts, and with this they paid for the building and the kingdom. And the fasts were long, and they mortified themselves before the god. And this was their fast: nine persons or men would fast, and nine would be prostrate in prayer and burn copal; and thirteen men would fast, and another thirteen would be in prayer and burn copal before the god Tohil. And they ate only sapotes, matasanos and jocotes, and they ate no tortillas. Whether there were seventeen men praying or seventeen fasting, they did not eat; and truly great was the fast they kept, and this was a sign of the lords' command. Nor did they sleep with women, but they kept themselves alone in continence, and they were fasting in the house of the god all day long, and only stayed in prayer, prostrate, burning copal. In this they were occupied, and there they stayed night and day weeping, asking for the light and life of their vassals, and also for their kingdom; and they raised their faces to the sky. And these were the petitions they made before the god, and this the weeping of their hearts:

"Oh you, beauty of the day, you, Huracán, you, Heart of the Sky and of the Earth, you, giver of our glory, and you, giver too of our sons and daughters: move and turn your glory hither, and grant that my sons and daughters may live and grow, and that those you sustain and nourish may multiply and increase, and those who call on you on the road, by the rivers and in the ravines, beneath the trees and vines. And give them their sons and daughters, and let them meet no misfortune or ill luck, and let them not be deceived; let them not stumble or fall, nor fornicate, nor be judged in any court; let them not fall on the high side or the low side of the road, nor let any blow come before them. Set them on a good and beautiful road; let them have no misfortune or ill luck from your hair. Oh, may the ways of those you sustain and nourish be good in your presence! You, Heart of the Sky, you, Heart of the Earth, you, Bundle of Glory, you, Tohil, Avilix and Hacavitz, womb of the sky, womb of the earth and four corners: let there be only peace in your presence, you god!"

So the lords would say when those nine, thirteen and seventeen men fasted, their hearts weeping through the days over their vassals and also over their wives and their children, when each of the lords performed his office. And this was the price by which light and life were bought, and by which lordship was bought, which was the command of the chiefs and lords. And they wept two by two, and took turns carrying the town on their shoulders with all the Quichés. And one was the beginning of the traditions, and the beginning of those who are fed and sustained; and those of Tanub and Ylocab did likewise, with those of Rabinal and the Cakchiquels, and those of Quiquinaha and of Tuhala and Vchabaha. And one was the custom of all in the Quiché, and so they reigned; and they did not begrudge the gifts of the one who fed and sustained them, but only saw to eating and drinking. And not for nothing did they subdue them and seize the empire and its glory and greatness; and so the peoples, small and great, were subdued. They paid a great price; they brought precious stones and silver, jades and green feathers; and the tribute of all the peoples was now established. And they came into the presence of the wonder-working kings Cucumatz and Cotuha, and into the presence of Quicab and Cavizimah, great lords of throne and house, and great and lofty men. It was not little that they did, and not few the peoples they conquered.

Many ranks of peoples came to pay tribute to the Quiché, and their deaths were much mourned, and the Quiché was exalted by them; and its greatness did not rise up just like that. This Cucumatz was the beginning of the greatness of the kingdom, and so he was the beginning of the Quiché being made great. And now we shall tell of the generations of the lords and their names; we shall now tell all of them again.
